key_insight: EyeRobot 2.0 shows that precise bimanual manipulation can be improved by actively moving the camera's gaze to a chosen 3D point, rather than relying on wrist-mounted cameras. It combines physical eye-like attention with foveated processing to focus compute on the most relevant part of the scene.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of achieving fine-grained robot manipulation without using wrist cameras, which are often costly, restrictive, or unavailable. It aims to maintain precise visual tracking and task-relevant detail using only a single stereo camera.
method: Uses Active Visual Fixation (AVF) to swivel two virtual eye viewpoints so both center on the same 3D fixation point in the scene.
Applies foveal image processing by allocating more visual tokens to the image center, emphasizing high-value details near the fixation point.
Coordinates gaze and perception to support precise bimanual manipulation with a single stereo camera setup.
impact: This approach offers a simpler and potentially more robust alternative to wrist-camera-based manipulation systems. For practitioners, it suggests a path to lower-hardware, compute-efficient robots that still retain strong visual precision for dexterous tasks.

paper_title: EyeRobot 2.0: Active Gaze for Precise Manipulation without Wrist Cameras
paper_authors: Kush Hari, Justin Kerr, Nidhya Shivakumar, Samarth Mahapatra, Carmelo Sferrazza
